headline: GOLD-ANTIMONY SHOOTS TO 250m DEPTH — Southern Cross Hits 26.2 g/t Au in First Deep Drill at Historic Redcastle; 11 Rigs Running, 71 Holes Pending (TSXV:SXGC)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Southern Cross Gold
snippet: Southern Cross Gold Consolidated (TSXV: SXGC | ASX: SX2) reported 26.2 g/t gold over 0.14 m from 112.98 m depth and 15.4 g/t Au over 0.22 m from 321.84 m in drill hole SDDRE016 at the Laura prospect — the first-ever deep drilling beneath the historic Redcastle goldfield in Victoria, 64 km northwest of its flagship Sunday Creek project. The results confirm Costerfield-style gold-antimony mineralization extending over more than 250 m of vertical extent, adding a new district-scale target to a company already running 11 drill rigs across a fully funded 200,000-metre program through Q1 2027 with results pending from 71 holes.

headline: AUSTRALIA'S NEW GOLD GIANT — Genesis & Vault Seal A$12.6B Merger, 600-700K oz/yr, Third-Largest ASX Producer; A$2B in Synergies, November Close (ASX:GMD/VAU)
snippet: Genesis Minerals Ltd. (ASX: GMD) and Vault Minerals Ltd. (ASX: VAU) agreed to merge in an A$12.6 billion (~US$9B) deal creating Australia's third-largest gold producer with 600,000–700,000 ounces of annual output from Western Australian operations — the deal closed after rival bidder Regis Resources withdrew on July 13. Vault shareholders receive 0.7629 Genesis shares plus A$0.475 cash per share (a 15.7% premium to Vault's July 3 close), with A$2 billion in post-tax cost synergies and capital savings targeted over 10 years; the scheme meeting is expected September–October 2026 for a November close.

headline: GOLD SURGES 1.6%, SILVER FOLLOWS — June CPI 3.5% Shocks Below 4.2% Prior; Fed Rate-Hike Odds Collapse to 30%, Dollar Falls, Mining Stocks Rally
snippet: U.S. June CPI came in at 3.5% year-on-year — sharply below May's 4.2% and below the 3.8% consensus — triggering a 1.6% gold surge to $4,070 and a silver bounce to $58.45 as traders unwound rate-hike bets: odds of a Fed hike at the July 28–29 meeting fell from nearly 40% to 30%. Core CPI also missed at 2.6% vs. 2.9% prior, and consumer prices fell 0.4% month-on-month for the first monthly deflation reading since 2020, reversing the Iran-Hormuz selloff and reopening the bull case for precious metals and mining equities into the second half.

headline: GOLD HOLDS $4,000 FLOOR AS PPI COOLS — June Producer Prices Fall 0.3%, Annual Rate Slips to 5.5%; Dual CPI/PPI Softness Reduces Fed Pressure
snippet: Spot gold traded near $4,061 Wednesday morning after June producer price index data showed final demand fell 0.3% — goods prices down 1.4%, annual PPI easing to 5.5% — adding confirmation to Tuesday's CPI-driven recovery and anchoring gold above the $4,000 psychological floor. The back-to-back soft inflation prints reduce pressure on the Fed for an imminent rate hike, though oil prices and Treasury yields remain elevated from ongoing Strait of Hormuz tension, keeping silver near $58.14 and the recovery somewhat restrained below the $4,090–$4,140 resistance zone.

headline: ISS BACKS EQUINOX-ORLA MEGA-DEAL — US$5.1B Gold Merger Creates 1.1M oz/yr North American Producer; Shareholders Vote July 22, Proxy Deadline Monday (TSX:EQX/ORLA)
snippet: Independent proxy advisory firms including ISS recommended Equinox Gold shareholders vote FOR the business combination with Orla Mining — a US$5.1 billion deal that would create a senior North American gold producer with 1.1 million ounces of 2026 production across six mines in the U.S., Mexico, and Nicaragua, with a pipeline to potentially 1.9 million ounces annually. The shareholder special meeting is July 22 with the proxy deadline Monday July 20; existing Equinox holders would retain approximately 67% of the combined entity, which boards of both companies unanimously endorse.

headline: ATMOSPHERIC RIVER THREATENS CHILE'S COPPER BELT — Flood Alert Covers Open-Pit Mines, Roads, Ports; Sector Already Down 19-34% YoY on Grade Decline and Drought
snippet: Chilean officials met with copper mining companies July 14 to prepare for a rare winter atmospheric river expected to bring prolonged flooding to the country's key copper production region, with open-pit mines, access roads, and port operations at potential risk. The weather threat compounds an already-stressed sector: BHP's Spence mine fell 34.4% in Q1 2026, Codelco's El Teniente dropped 26.5%, and Collahuasi declined 19.3% in May — each citing combinations of a 14-year Atacama drought (reservoirs at 30% capacity), structural ore grade decline, and the transition from oxide to sulfide mining in a country supplying roughly 50% of global copper exports.

headline: VANECK: GOLD STOCK PULLBACK IS 'NOISE' — Mining Equities +46% YTD vs S&P 500's +22%; Record Cash Flow at Sub-$2,000 AISC Makes Miners the 'Standout Trade'
snippet: VanEck's gold analyst Imaru Casanova dismissed the recent correction in gold mining stocks as short-term noise, arguing the sector remains the most compelling trade of the current cycle: with gold averaging $4,700/oz through 2026 and all-in sustaining costs below $2,000/oz sector-wide, miners are generating record cash flow even at today's lower $4,060 spot price. Mining equities are still up nearly 46% year-to-date against the S&P 500's 22%, yet valuations remain historically low relative to prevailing gold prices — a divergence Casanova frames as a buy window, not a warning sign.

headline: BOFA CUTS 2026 GOLD FORECAST 14% TO $4,360 — But Miners Trade 19% Below NAV, Earnings Yield at 20-Year Sector High; 'Compelling Value' Case Intact
snippet: Bank of America lowered its 2026 average gold price forecast 14% to US$4,360 per ounce, citing expectations for three Federal Reserve rate hikes this year — but the bank's equity team simultaneously flagged gold miners as compelling value: the sector trades at a 19% discount to net asset values, the earnings yield is the highest of any sector at 12.0% (the most attractive relative to the S&P 500 in 20 years), and miner free cash flow is 10x the 2020 level. Even at the reduced forecast, gold is implied to trade well above today's $4,060 spot price — a structurally bullish message hidden inside a bearish headline.

headline: UTAH HEAP-LEACH GOLD HITS OUTSIDE THE PEA PIT — Revival Mercur South Zone: 1.65 g/t Au Over 30.5m, 'Potential Expansion Beyond PEA'; 18,000m Campaign Running (TSXV:RVG)
snippet: Revival Gold Inc. (TSXV: RVG) released initial results from the South Mercur area of its Mercur Gold Project in Utah, with hole RM26-204 returning 1.65 g/t gold over 30.5 metres from 128 metres depth, alongside 0.92 g/t Au over 30.5 metres in a nearby hole — among the project's highest grades encountered in heap-leachable material and outside the existing preliminary economic assessment pit shell. Results are from the first 13 of 74 completed holes in a fully funded 18,000-metre 2026 drill program, with the South Mercur intercepts suggesting resource expansion potential in low-strip, shallow oxide material amenable to low-cost heap leach processing.

headline: SILVER: SIXTH DEFICIT YEAR, TWO CATALYSTS AHEAD — GoldSilver.com Eyes FOMC July 29 as Pivot Point; 46M oz Shortfall Intact, LBMA Consensus at $79.57
snippet: GoldSilver.com's July 2026 silver outlook identifies two near-term catalysts for a metal currently trading at $58.55 — 52% below its January all-time high of $121.64: the June CPI beat has already shifted Fed rate-hike odds toward a hold, and the July 28–29 FOMC decision is now the decisive binary for second-half direction. The structural case — silver's sixth consecutive annual supply deficit totalling 46.3 million ounces, with 58% of demand tied to growing industrial uses including solar and EVs — remains fully intact regardless of Fed timing, with LBMA analyst consensus at $79.57 and JPMorgan targeting $81 per ounce for the year.
